## **All about ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)**

It is not wrong to say that in today’s time, [ETL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extract,_transform,_load) has become the foundation that carries the load of the data-driven market. It encompasses three steps — extraction, transformation, and loading. To help you understand the concept of ETL, here we are briefly explaining all the three steps:

Extract: The first step involves the extraction of data from disparate sources and ensuring that all the relevant data is collected into a single space. The data is collected directly from its original source and is in its rawest form.

Transform: In the second step of ETL, the collected data is cleaned and formatted into the desired format. The goal is to make the data easy-to-understand for the end-user. The step is carried out, maintaining the quality and integrity of data, along with removing duplicates & errors and sorting the data into the predetermined categories.

Load: Here comes the last step where the formatted data gets loaded into the target location, which can be your preferred data warehouse or business intelligence tool. After the last step, you get access to the data, which is ready for analysis and reporting.

## **Benefits of ETL**

-   **Automation that saves time:** The popularity of ETL is owing to its ability to automate the [process of aggregating](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-aggregation-tools/), transforming, and assembling the data. Users no longer need to manually perform the data integration process that saves them a lot of time and makes them divert their focus on other core processes.
-   **Zero chances of human errors:** Humans are perfectionists but no matter how hard they try, it’s almost impossible to minimize the risk of manual errors to zero. Making a single mistake in the early stage of data analytics can cost a lot to organizations. With an effective ETL tool, you can avoid errors and power up your data integration process.
-   **Complex data is no longer an issue:** ETL helps you wave goodbye to data complexity. With an efficient ETL tool, you can add location coordinates, device IDs, customers’ names, seller URLs, and time zones to make the data sets fall into their respective categories.
-   **Weave your path towards better decision-making:** By automating the [process of data integration](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-integration-everything-you-need-to-know/) and eliminating the chances of errors, an ETL tool ensures that you get the highest quality of data to perform analysis. With the right information at your end, you can make the best decisions to help your business thrive.
-   **Higher ROI:** One of the best benefits of ETL is that it saves your time, efforts, and resources. By using [ETL in the long run](https://datachannel.co/blogs/etl-best-practices/), you can boost your productivity and expect a higher ROI.

## **All About Data Integration**

Data integration is a combination of various processes, including ETL. The process involves collecting data from different sources (both internal and external) and devices and loading it into a warehouse for the purpose of cleansing, organizing, and analyzing. With effective data integration, you can get a vivid and unified picture of your business data that further helps you make decisions that can drive better results.

#### **The increasing need for data integration**

The amount of data collected from several sources is increasing at a faster pace. Data is the most valuable resource a company can possess to streamline its operations and ensure growth.

Different businesses implement different strategies focused on utilizing the data efficiently and completing applications as soon as possible. But, are they able to use data to its full capacity? If you have the same question in mind, let us explain it to you.

As per a survey, around 60% of companies lack a feasible and precisely functional business strategy that can result in favorable outcomes.

But with data integration, the problem can be solved. By using the best data integration tools, you can access crucial business data in real-time and run analysis to derive actionable insights. Here are a few other benefits of data integration:

-   Reduce complexity in data
-   Add value to the data collected from different systems
-   Centralize the data for making it more valuable and easy to use
-   Simplifies the collaboration among various business systems
-   Provide meaningful insights on which better decisions are made
-   Facilitates better communication among different departments across an organization
-   Update data in real-time along with maintaining data security & safety
-   Delivers a better customer experience****

## **Conclusion**

ETL and data integration are two different ways to reach the same goal. Both processes have the potential to help professionals to get their relevant data combined and make it ready for analysis as seamlessly as possible. With the right data in hand, driving valuable insights becomes an easy task.

The best ETL and data integration tools give you the freedom to explore the data, transform it in any specified format, and derive meaningful insights from it. The insights give you the power to predict the future and make business decisions that can help you skyrocket your ROI.
